learning_goal: Trace the vertebral canal from the foramen magnum to the sacral hiatus, say where the cord ends in an adult and in a newborn, and give the reason lumbar puncture is done at L3/4 or L4/5.

structures.name: central canal of spinal cord
structures.label: Central canal — upper 34 mm only
structures.narration: This thread is the central canal, the lumen down the middle of the cord — but the model holds only its topmost 34 millimetres, level with the atlas and axis and reaching up into the skull. It does not run down the back, so do not read its lower end as the end of the cord.

structures.name: atlas
structures.label: C1 — atlas
structures.narration: A ring rather than a vertebra — no body, no spinous process, and it carries the skull. The canal is at its widest here, which is why the cord usually escapes in a fracture of the atlas. The cervical enlargement lies lower down.

structures.name: axis
structures.label: C2 — axis
structures.narration: The dens rises from its body into the ring of the atlas above. The canal is still wide at this level. The cervical enlargement of the cord lies well below it: about the C4 to T1 vertebral levels.

structures.name: third cervical vertebra
structures.label: C3
structures.narration: A cervical ring, wide and triangular. The cervical enlargement has not started yet at this level — it begins at about C4, just below.

structures.name: fourth cervical vertebra
structures.label: C4
structures.narration: A cervical ring. The canal is wide and triangular here, with the cervical enlargement of the cord inside it. It is widest of all at the atlas, which is why the cord usually escapes a fracture up there.

structures.name: fifth cervical vertebra
structures.label: C5
structures.narration: A cervical ring. The canal is wide and triangular here, with the cervical enlargement of the cord inside it. It is widest of all at the atlas, which is why the cord usually escapes a fracture up there.

structures.name: sixth cervical vertebra
structures.label: C6
structures.narration: A cervical ring. The canal is wide and triangular here, with the cervical enlargement of the cord inside it. It is widest of all at the atlas, which is why the cord usually escapes a fracture up there.

structures.name: seventh cervical vertebra
structures.label: C7
structures.narration: A cervical ring. The canal is wide and triangular here, with the cervical enlargement of the cord inside it. It is widest of all at the atlas, which is why the cord usually escapes a fracture up there.

structures.name: first thoracic vertebra
structures.label: T1
structures.narration: The first thoracic ring, and the lower end of the cervical enlargement. Below this level the canal narrows and rounds off, and the room to spare around the cord runs out.

structures.name: second thoracic vertebra
structures.label: T2
structures.narration: A thoracic ring. The canal is narrowest and most circular in the thorax, so there is least room to spare around the cord here.

structures.name: first lumbar vertebra
structures.label: L1 — the cord ends about here
structures.narration: In the adult the cord tapers to the conus medullaris at the lower border of L1 or the upper border of L2. Below this line the canal holds nerve roots only.

structures.name: second lumbar vertebra
structures.label: L2
structures.narration: The last level at which cord may still be present. Everything below is cauda equina.

structures.name: third lumbar vertebra
structures.label: L3
structures.narration: Below the cord. The canal here holds the cauda equina bathed in cerebrospinal fluid — roots float away from a needle instead of being pierced by it.

structures.name: fourth lumbar vertebra
structures.label: L4
structures.narration: Below the cord. The canal here holds the cauda equina bathed in cerebrospinal fluid — roots float away from a needle instead of being pierced by it.

structures.name: fifth lumbar vertebra
structures.label: L5
structures.narration: Below the cord. The canal here holds the cauda equina bathed in cerebrospinal fluid — roots float away from a needle instead of being pierced by it.

structures.name: sacrum
structures.label: Sacrum
structures.narration: The canal continues into the sacrum and ends at the sacral hiatus. The dural sac itself stops around S2.

structures.name: intervertebral disk of third lumbar vertebra
structures.label: L3/4 disc — a puncture level
structures.narration: One of the two spaces used for lumbar puncture. The needle passes between the spines of L3 and L4, well below the end of the cord.

structures.name: intervertebral disk of fourth lumbar vertebra
structures.label: L4/5 disc — a puncture level
structures.narration: The other usual space. A line joining the highest points of the iliac crests crosses the body of L4, and that is how the level is found at the bedside.

views.title: One long tube
views.narration: Stack the vertebral foramina and they line up into one continuous tube — the vertebral canal. It begins at the foramen magnum, follows every curve of the column, and ends at the sacral hiatus. The cord lies inside it, wrapped in three membranes and floating in cerebrospinal fluid.

views.title: What fills the ring
views.narration: Cut across at a mid-thoracic level. The ring behind the body is the canal. Inside it, from outside in: fat and veins in the epidural space, then dura, then arachnoid, then cerebrospinal fluid in the subarachnoid space, and the cord in the middle held by pia. The thoracic canal is the tightest of all, which is why cord compression shows itself early here.

views.title: The canal in the midline
views.narration: Split the column in the midline and the canal reads as a single passage with the bodies in front of it and the arches behind. The bright thread near the top is the central canal — the only piece of cord tissue in this model, and only 34 millimetres of it, at the atlas and axis. Everything else about the cord here is description, not display: it would fill the upper two thirds of this passage and stop, leaving the lower third to roots and fluid.

views.title: Where the cord stops
views.narration: The cord ends as the conus medullaris at the lower border of L1 in the adult, and about L3 in the newborn. Below that the canal holds only the cauda equina in cerebrospinal fluid — which is why a lumbar puncture goes in at L3/4 or L4/5. That level is read off the vertebrae here; there is no cord model to show it ending.

views.title: How the nerves get out
views.narration: Between every two vertebrae, the notches on the pedicles leave a window — the intervertebral foramen — and a pair of spinal nerves leaves through it. Thirty-one pairs in all. Because the cord ends high, the lower roots must run downwards inside the canal to reach their own foramen; that bundle is the cauda equina.

views.title: Where the needle goes
views.narration: Lumbar puncture is done at L3/4 or L4/5. The cord has already ended at L1, so the needle enters the lumbar cistern — cerebrospinal fluid with the cauda equina floating in it, and roots slide aside rather than tear. Find the level by the intercristal line, which crosses L4. In a child go lower still, because the cord ends lower.

views.title: Room to spare, region by region
views.narration: Look at the size of the ring in each region. Wide and triangular in the neck, narrow and round in the thorax, wide again in the loin. Where the ring is narrowest the cord is most vulnerable, and where it is widest the canal is holding either an enlargement or a bundle of roots.

gaps: THE SPINAL CORD ITSELF HAS NO MODEL. The catalog holds 934 meshes and not one of them is the cord: the only entry in its neighbourhood is the central canal, a thread down the middle of the cord. The scene is built on the bony canal, which is complete, and uses the central canal to show where the cord runs. That is honest but it is not the cord, and it is the reason this scene is candidate and not ready.

Because the cord is missing, so is everything the cord teaches at this level: the cervical and lumbosacral enlargements, the conus medullaris and the filum terminale, and grey matter against white. All are narrated. The moment a cord model exists it becomes the subject of the TRACE_STRUCTURE in beat 2 in place of concept:spinal-cord, with no other edit.

The extent of the central canal mesh HAS now been measured (tools/derive-vertebra-landmarks.mjs shares the STL reader used for it), and the answer changed this scene. the central canal mesh spans Z 1470.8 to 1504.4 — 33.6 mm, level with C1 and C2 and continuing up into the skull. It is not present at C5 or anywhere below. It therefore cannot stand in for the course of the cord, and the earlier wording that read it as "the axis of the cord, wherever this runs" was wrong: it runs for 34 mm at the top of the neck. The SHOW_RELATIONSHIP tying it to L1 has been removed, its terms no longer claim "spinal cord" or "conus medullaris", and the cord's termination is taught from the vertebrae, which are measured.

No meninges in the catalog: dura, arachnoid and pia, the epidural and subarachnoid spaces, and the lumbar cistern are all narrated over bone. The layers a needle crosses are the exam question and they cannot be shown.
No spinal nerves, roots or cauda equina exist (the catalog's only nerves are the two optic nerves), so 'How the nerves get out' shows the foramen and describes what passes through it.

The coccyx is not a separate model: it is segmented together with the sacrum in one mesh (measured: 104.0 mm of sacrum above a 41.3 mm midline tail). The canal is therefore followed to the sacrum, and the sacral hiatus — at the bottom of that same mesh — is narrated rather than labelled.

NO VASCULATURE VIEW, AND NONE IS AUTHORABLE. CURRICULUM.json requires a `vasculature` view of this structure ("segmental blood supply"); this scene has none, and until now the omission was not recorded here even though six others were. Re-searched the catalog this run under vertebral, spinal, radicular, segmental, medullary, artery, arteria, intercostal, lumbar and basivertebral: the 934 meshes contain no vertebral artery, no anterior or posterior spinal artery, no radicular or segmental medullary artery, no posterior intercostal or lumbar artery, and no vertebral venous plexus. The nearest vessels in the catalog are the aortic segments (FMA3736, FMA3768, FMA3784) and the renal and iliac trunks, none of which reaches the canal. The artery of Adamkiewicz, the watershed at the mid-thoracic cord, and the internal vertebral venous plexus that carries prostatic and breast metastases to the spine therefore cannot be drawn or even approximated, and a beat moded `vasculature` would be an empty stage. Recorded as a gap rather than authored as a hollow view. This is one of the two reasons the scene stays candidate.
